key_insight: Maestro improves Lean proof development by diagnosing failures and revising the overall proof plan instead of repeatedly decomposing stuck lemmas.
engineering_relevance: Global coordination can make formal verification and verified code synthesis more robust by directing failed obligations toward guidance, correction, replanning, or code repair.
method: Prover agents report why proof attempts failed.
A coordinator uses whole-proof context to guide agents, correct false lemmas, or retract and replan flawed subtrees.
For verified code synthesis, checked counterexamples trigger code repair.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation with four frontier LLMs on seven mathematics and three software verification benchmarks, including 34/48 arXivLean proofs versus 19/48 for the native agent, plus 669/672 PutnamBench and 59/60 Lean-IMO-Bench.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify coordination overhead or compute cost, so the efficiency of the reported gains remains unclear.
paper_title: Maestro: Agentic Formal Proof Development by Coordination
